title: Tôi bị dị ứng đậu phộng
pronunciation: toy bee zee oong dow fohng
summary: Different ways to say "I am allergic to peanuts" in Vietnam, with the safe phrase, useful variants, and nearby next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this before you order when peanuts are the main food risk. Lead with the allergy warning, then ask about ingredients if needed. Use the nearby forms below when tone, setting, or politeness changes.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Tôi bị dị ứng đậu phộng is the safest default for "I am allergic to peanuts". Use this before you order when peanuts are the main food risk. Say it slowly, then point, show your phone, or hold up the item if the other person needs more context.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Vietnamese food interactions move fast, so pointing and short phrases protect the order.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this before you order when peanuts are the main food risk. Use it in ordering, adjusting dishes, and checking ingredients when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: For allergies and dietary limits, use the clearest version and confirm visually if possible.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Point to the dish or ingredient while speaking. It helps when tone marks or dish names are hard to pronounce.
